text: The latest proposal is the Project Paper for a proposed second additional credit and restructuring of RISE (PPIAF000398, dated 2026-09-30). Compared with the project as it stands (and the original PAD):

Objectives: no change. The PDO stays as revised by the first AF in February 2025, "to improve rural road connectivity, generate jobs, strengthen road management capacity and support emergency response in selected areas, incorporating community engagement approaches" (AF2 paper pp. 1-2, 10 para. 20). That 2025 revision had replaced the PAD's PDO on rural road access, employment and capacity (PAD p. 23).

Components: no change to scope; the six components remain. The AF replenishes Component 1 by US$25 million, restoring the US$25 million moved to the CERC (Component 5) when it was triggered on 3 September 2024. Component 6, Restoration of Critical Connectivity (US$100 million), was added by AF1 (AF2 paper pp. 1-2, Table 1 p. 5).

Results framework (Table 3, pp. 7-9): direct-users targets set (7,031,928 people, of which 3,684,533 female and 2,384,856 youth); a new corporate indicator on people benefiting from climate-resilient infrastructure (same targets); 'civil works jobs created' replaced by the corporate 'more and better-paid job equivalents' (target 140,335); CERC interventions target cut from 7 to 6; km of rural roads improved cut from 535 to 276.01 (regional 135 to 104.61, district 400 to 171.4); CBRM routine maintenance from 23,000 km to 15,000 km; bottleneck improvements from 4,500 km to 2,373 km; the National Rural Roads Plan becomes a National District Roads Plan; the road safety data system indicator and the code-of-conduct indicator are dropped; people employed under CBRM raised from 19,000 to 23,500 person-years; Component 6 targets set (11 regional and 84 district cut-off areas restored). The paper says the reductions align outputs with the financing gap the midterm review found (p. 7, paras. 11-12).

Financing: an additional IDA credit of US$25 million, taking total financing from US$450 million (original US$350 million including US$50 million Government counterpart, plus AF1 US$100 million) to US$475 million (Table 1, p. 5). The midterm review had found a US$90 million gap (US$65 million for existing activities and US$25 million for the CERC) (p. 2), so the AF covers only part of it.
Closing date: extended by 18 months, from 30 June 2027 (the PAD's original closing date, PAD p. 8) to 31 December 2028 (p. 4, para. 8).
Implementation and fiduciary arrangements, safeguards standards and the Substantial risk rating are unchanged (pp. 1, 10).

right_sources: Uses the 2026-09-30 project paper (PPIAF000398) and compares with the original PAD (or the AF1 paper) for the baseline.
